results.text:
Under GRAP Stage IV, closure of all non-essential highly polluting industries
operating on unapproved fuels is mandatory. Entry of trucks into the NCR is
banned except those carrying essential commodities or running on LNG/CNG/BS-VI
diesel or electric. Public, municipal, and private offices may operate at 50%
capacity with work-from-home for the rest. Construction and demolition is
completely halted, including for essential public projects. State governments
may take a decision on closure of schools and colleges.

Mandated switching of industries in the NCR from coal and pet-coke to piped
natural gas (PNG) reduced sulphur dioxide and particulate emissions from the
affected industrial clusters. Compliance monitoring under the Air Act, 1981,
combined with closure directions for non-compliant units, was central to the
outcome.

NCAP covers 131 non-attainment cities and million-plus cities that did not meet
the National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) over a five-year period.
Each city is required to prepare and implement a city-specific Clean Air Action
Plan addressing sources such as road dust, vehicular emissions, industrial
emissions, biomass burning, and construction dust.

- Good (0-50): Minimal impact. Air quality is satisfactory for all.
- Satisfactory (51-100): Minor breathing discomfort to sensitive people.
- Moderate (101-200): Breathing discomfort to people with lung and heart
  disease. Sensitive groups should reduce prolonged outdoor exertion.
- Poor (201-300): Breathing discomfort to most people on prolonged exposure.
- Very Poor (301-400): Respiratory illness on prolonged exposure. Avoid
  outdoor physical activity.
- Severe (401-500): Serious health impact even on healthy people; serious
  effect on those with existing diseases.
